title: Plastic Alternatives
desc: Understand materials that can replace single-use plastic, how to test them honestly, and how to plan a small product switch.
outcomes: Explain plastic types and the problem of waste.
Test an alternative for use and cost.
Judge claims such as biodegradable and compostable.
Plan a product switch for a small business.
task: Choose one single-use plastic item, test two alternatives, compare cost and impact, and write a switch plan with customer message.
condition: Samples of items, a scale and basic tools, a spreadsheet, two peers and a mentor. Safe, non-food-contact tests unless approved.
standard: Tests are repeatable; claims are checked against recognised definitions; cost per use is shown; end-of-life route exists locally; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Shop owners, packaging buyers, students, municipal staff.
evidence: test sheet, comparison table, switch plan
modules: Single-use items are used for minutes and last for centuries.
Reduce first, reuse second, recycle third.
Refill stations cut bottle use more than any new material.
Audit the plastic you use in a week.
Some types are widely recycled, some not.
Mixed and dirty plastic is hard to recycle.
PET bottles are often recycled; film is not.
Paper, glass, metal, plant fibres, starch-based, compostable blends.
Each has a cost and an impact.
A cafe moves to returnable cups.
Strength, leak, heat, shelf life, cost per use.
A starch bag tears at 3 kg; paper holds 5 kg.
Raw material, making, transport, use, end of life.
Reuse items win after enough uses.
A glass jar needs 12 uses to beat plastic.
Biodegradable and compostable are not the same.
A bag labelled "eco" has no standard; the buyer asks for a test report.
Cost per use, not per piece.
A refill discount repays within 20 uses.
Plastic bags fall by 70% in a month.
quiz: Strength, leak, heat or shelf life.
Material, making, transport, use, end of life.
rubric: Every claim linked to a dated record and checked by a peer
Checked, dated and explained to others
next: water management, greenhouse gas auditing, biofuels.
local: Packaging, food-contact and waste rules differ by place.
ladder: L1: learner can name plastic problems.
L4: learner can compare life cycles.
L6: learner can lead a switch.
